title: Fifteen more schools: J.S. Jenks, Russell Byers, Cook-Wissahickon, Robert Morris, C.W. Henry, Mastery Thomas, Emlen, Wright, J.B. Kelly, Edmonds, Willard, Lea, Rhoads, Juniata Park and Greenberg
text: Each has its own page with what runs there, what picks up from it and what’s a short walk away. New to the site are Urban Youth King & Queens, which runs before and after care inside C.W. Henry, Cook-Wissahickon, Houston and J.B. Kelly; Caring People Alliance’s free program at Robert Morris; Russell Byers’s own after-school program; the two aftercare providers at Mastery Thomas; the Boys & Girls Clubs at Emlen and Greenberg; LEGACY’s Champions on the Rise and Shoot Basketballs NOT People at Wright; Zhang Sah’s program inside J.B. Kelly; IAC and YMWIC at Edmonds; Early Life Academy and WES Health at Willard; Penn’s UACS program at Lea, where Parent Infant Center also picks up; Safe Haven and Rebel Arts at Rhoads; the YMCA and After-School All-Stars at Juniata Park; and the Philly KiDZ Initiative at Greenberg. Russell Byers and Mastery Thomas keep their own calendars, so their pages go by their own days off, not the District’s. That makes 31 schools.

title: Bingo in Kids’ Playground
text: Each child now gets a bingo card for the school year, and a new one for the summer. Classes you confirm and things they do in the Playground daub the squares. Five in a row wins something for their bulb to wear, and the whole card turns the card’s own pin diamond, with a certificate you can print for the fridge.

title: Kid’s Corner is now Kids’ Playground
text: The part of your account made for your children has a new name: Kids’ Playground. Everything in it stays the same, from pins and the map to Eddie’s showdowns, and the old address still takes you there.

title: Two more schools: Independence Charter and Greenfield
text: Each has its own page: 13 programs run at ICS or pick up from it, and 12 at or from Greenfield, most of them around Rittenhouse Square. New to the site are Beacon Center, Evolve Dance, Martial Posture, Yous Fitfulness and ICS’s own after-school program, and ZAZZ and Koresh now show their after-school classes with pickup. ICS keeps its own calendar, so its page goes by ICS’s days off, not the District’s. That makes 16 schools.

title: Lists that start from your school or your street
text: The after-school list now starts by asking for your child’s school. The day-camp, weekend and summer lists, and each day off’s page, ask for your ZIP code and put what’s closest to you first, with everything else still on the list below. Answer once and every list remembers it on your device. The week builder starts from your school too.

title: Eddie in sunglasses, and Philly showdowns
text: Finish planning a week, a month of days off or the whole summer, and Eddie Bulboa slides across the screen in his sunglasses: too cool for school. In Kids’ Playground, the showdowns are all Philly now, eleven of them: a race up the Art Museum steps, a cheesesteak eating contest, a Ben Franklin kite fly-off, a Liberty Bell ring-off, a water ice slurp-off, a Boathouse Row regatta, a Mummers strut-off, a hoagie build-off, a pothole dodge, a soft pretzel stack-off and a mural paint-off.

title: Three more summer camps
text: Kids on 12th’s Center City summer camp (ages 3–11), STEM Prep’s summer camp in Fishtown (ages 3–10), and Camp Nerd Street, a video game and esports camp on North Broad (ages 8–13). Only Kids on 12th has posted full details so far, and those are for 2026. Follow any of them and you’ll get one email when it posts summer 2027.

title: A new school: Houston, in Mount Airy
text: Henry H. Houston School has its own page now, asked for by parents: three programs that pick up there at dismissal (Philly Art Center, the Philadelphia School of Circus Arts and Zhang Sah), and what’s a short walk away. That makes 14 schools.

title: Surprises in every neighborhood, and Account Features
text: Every neighborhood on the Kids’ Playground map now hides one or two little Philly things, from a soft pretzel and water ice to a trolley, a stoop cat and an open hydrant. The first class there finds one, and another class there finds the next. The Parent Portal’s Kids’ Playground card now says whether your kids have started. And there’s a new Account Features section in the menu, with a page each on calendar and sharing, the Parent Portal and Kids’ Playground, so you can show a friend what an account does.

title: Kids’ Playground: Eddie’s welcome, a Repeater Reward and secret spots
text: The first time your kid opens Kids’ Playground, Eddie Bulboa shows them round: making their bulb, the pins they already have, the map and how to pick a favorite. Going back to a class your kid loves now counts: each day a week, each term and each week of the same camp earns the new Repeater Reward pin and points toward the next level. Set how many times in the grown-ups’ corner, and Kids’ Playground asks when your plans show more. The map has secret spots that turn up as they go to more classes nearby, and the showdown now simply asks which class they had more fun at. Tried it out yourself first? “Start over” on your kid’s card in the Parent Portal gives them a fresh start.

title: Signing in: two weeks at a time
text: To keep your plans and your kids’ names safe on a shared or lost device, a device now signs itself out after two weeks without a visit, and after 90 days however often it’s used. Signing back in is the same 6-digit code by email, or Google.

title: Kids’ Playground: dress-up, showdowns and grander pins
text: Each kid’s bulb now starts plain and unlocks things to wear as they level up, from shades and a bow tie to a cape, wings and a galaxy glow, and they choose what it wears. Pins get grander as they go from bronze to silver to gold. And the bulbs now race up the Art Museum steps, have glow-offs and dance-offs to pick a favorite, instead of boxing.

title: Your Parent Portal
text: The button in the menu is now Parent Portal. It opens on an overview of where to start, with how far each part has got: your kids’ week, the days off, the summer, your to-do list and your year calendar. My Profile sits beside it in the menu, and Kids’ Playground has a button of its own.

title: Kids’ Playground: a page for each of your kids
text: Every class and camp your kids go to now earns them something on a page of their own: shiny pins that go from bronze to gold, a cartoon map of Philly that clears as they explore it, and a lightbulb for every program, racing and dancing for the title of favorite. Eddie Bulboa, the bulb in our logo, shows them around. You say what counts, their favorites come first when you plan, and nothing on it is counted or recorded.

title: Co-parents, and sharing a week
text: Two parents can now share one set of plans: invite your co-parent from Plans & sharing, and you both see and change the same weeks, days off, summer and calendar. You can also share a kept week with one person, like a grandparent or a sitter.

title: Four more schools: Marian Anderson, Lingelbach, Childs and Bache-Martin
text: Each has its own page now: what runs in the building, which programs pick up at dismissal, and what’s a short walk away. That makes 13 schools. Two of the four were asked for by parents.

title: We’re open
text: Philly After School is out of preview as of today: eight schools east of Broad, 82 programs, 44 summer camps and every district day off, with planners that save to your profile. If your school isn’t here yet, ask for it and we’ll tell you when it’s up. And tell one parent at pickup.

title: Classes and camps go by age
text: Weekend classes, day camps and summer camps now filter by your child’s age, and after-school programs keep going by grade. Ages you keep on your account page, or give a child on the summer planner, become “My kids” on those lists.

title: Plans now save to your profile
text: When you’re signed in, your week, your days-off plan and your summer are now kept in your profile on their own, so they’re on your phone and your computer with nothing to press. Each planner has a “Take it out of my profile” link if you’d rather one stayed on a single device. The summer schedule also has a calendar view now.

title: A to-do list for camp sign-ups
text: Putting a camp on a day off isn’t the same as signing up for it, so each camp day in your days-off plan now has a “Signed up?” box. Tick it once you’ve registered and the day turns green. Everything still to sign up for is gathered on a To do page, with a link to each camp’s own page: it’s in the menu once you’re signed in, and on My kids’ calendar. A parent asked for this one.

title: Your plan, as a calendar
text: My kids’ calendar now opens as a month you can tap through, with each day off, camp week and date of your own on its day; the list is one tap away. The days-off planner has a calendar view too. The planners now ask you to sign in with a free account, and a plan you already made on this device is still there when you do. Finish planning a month and you may meet a dragon.

title: A page for every day off
text: Each day school is closed now has its own page with the camps that have posted that date, what they run and where they are. Open one from the days-off list, or from the next day off shown on the home page and on each school’s page.

title: Three more schools: Kirkbride, Southwark and Columbus Charter
text: Each has its own page now: what runs in the building, which programs pick up at dismissal, and what’s a short walk away. Columbus Charter is the first charter school here; its page covers the kindergarten to 4th grade building on Christian St.

title: Every kind of program, on one page
text: After school, weekend classes, camps on days off and summer camps each have their own list. A new page puts the four side by side, with how many of each there are, so you can start from the part of the year you’re filling.

title: Notifications on your phone, with no app
text: Sign-up dates can now come as a notification on your phone or computer, as well as or instead of the emails. Turn it on in your account. On an iPhone, add Philly After School to your Home Screen first; the page shows how.

title: Tell the next family how it’s going
text: Once a program has been on your week for a few weeks, we may ask if you’d write a short review. It takes about two minutes and helps the next family choose. You can say “not yet”, or “don’t ask about this one”.

title: My profile, and your account
text: My profile is one card now: you, your kids, your school, what you follow, your favorites, your schedules and calendars. To change any of it, go to your account. You can change the email address you sign in with there, too.

title: This week at your school
text: Each school’s page now shows the week ahead: days off and sign-ups. You can get it by email on Sunday mornings: keep your school in your account and turn it on under Emails.

title: Your own dates, and faster emails
text: Add picture day, pretzel day or a form that’s due to My kids’ calendar, for one child or everyone. Something weekly takes just a day of the week (every Wednesday), and your own dates can go on the month pictures. A sign-up date you follow is emailed the morning after it’s posted, then the day before and that morning, each with a link to stop that one listing.

title: Follow and favorites
text: Follow a program, a camp or your school and its dates come by email. Save a listing as a favorite to find it again. Both are listed on this page.

title: One page for every planner
text: The week, the days off and the summer, side by side, with what each one does.

title: My kids’ calendar
text: Everything you’ve planned for the year in one private calendar, with a file for your phone.
